Description

[Android Bug] Permanent Mic Distortion (Popping) Triggered by Thermal Throttling & Unrecoverable via Mute Toggle

Category: Bug Report / Mobile Audio Input

Issue Description:

There is a severe audio buffer underrun/deadlock issue with the microphone input on the VRChat Android client.

When launching the app on a cool device, the microphone works normally for the first few minutes. However, as the device heats up and CPU thermal throttling occurs, the microphone input permanently degrades into a continuous, rhythmic popping sound (sounding like a bouncing basketball or fast clicking).

Unlike minor audio glitches, toggling mute off and on does NOT fix or reset the audio stream once this state is reached. The mic remains broken indefinitely until the app is closed and the device cools down completely. This issue happens on both the built-in microphone and connected Bluetooth headsets.

Device Specs:

 * Device Model: Redmi K60

 * Android OS: Android 13

 * Audio Source: Built-in Microphone

 * VRChat Mobile Version: 2026.3.2p2-1903-26038eb883-Release

Reproduction Steps

Steps to Reproduce:

 * Launch VRChat on Redmi K60 (Android 13) from a cold start.

 * Unmute the mic and speak normally (audio is clear for 2–5 minutes).

 * Continue playing until the phone warms up under load and enters thermal throttling.

 * The microphone input permanently degrades into a continuous popping/stuttering noise.

 * Try toggling the mute button in the quick menu -> The audio stream fails to recover and stays broken.

 * The issue only disappears after closing the app, letting the device cool down, and restarting VRChat.

Suspected Cause & Feature Request:

This appears to be audio thread starvation or an unhandled buffer underrun within the Unity/RNNoise audio pipeline during CPU frequency throttling. Please implement a mechanism to fully re-initialize the audio capture device/buffer when the mic is toggled, or add a failsafe for audio thread starvation under thermal strain on Android

Details

- Category: 音频

- Frequency: Always
